diagnosis.summary: nightly run d1e21651 (2026-10-01) failed at the ingest step. The upstream customers.csv now has a new column, marketing_opt_in, that isn't in the raw contract. All contract columns are still there and the file parses cleanly. I've proposed a fix: ignore_extra_columns on customers for marketing_opt_in. The pipeline will be rerun to check it.

root_cause.explanation: Upstream added a new column, marketing_opt_in, to the customers landing file. Ingest compares the file header to the raw.customers contract and fails on any mismatch. Here the only mismatch is this extra column: no contract columns are missing, and there are no parse problems.

evidence.claim: Run d1e21651 failed at ingest with a schema mismatch on raw.customers: no missing columns, one unexpected column (marketing_opt_in).
The 2026-10-01 customers landing file has all contract columns plus marketing_opt_in, 30 rows and no parse problems.
The orders file for the same day matches the contract, so this is not a general bad delivery.
The runbook says an unexpected column with nothing missing means upstream added a column, and the fix is ignore_extra_columns.
The ingest config is at its defaults, so nothing is set to ignore the new column yet.

alternatives_considered: Column rename: ruled out because no contract column is missing.
Asking upstream to re-send the file: not appropriate, because adding a column looks like a deliberate, lasting change and the runbook says to adapt ingest instead.
Corrupt or partial file: ruled out because the file ends cleanly, has no parse problems and has normal rows.
A dbt model change: ruled out because the run failed at ingest, before any transform ran.

proposal.rationale: Upstream added a new non-contract column 'marketing_opt_in' to customers.csv; all contract columns are present and the file is otherwise well-formed (30 rows, no parse problems). Per runbook, a new non-contract column is handled by ignoring it at ingest.

applied: ingest now ignores upstream columns ['marketing_opt_in'] on raw.customers
